extraction.design: pooled analysis of prospective matched case-control sets
extraction.population: Men (prostate cancer cases and controls) from 15 prospective studies

sample_size.excerpt: Data were available for up to 11,239 cases (including 1654 advanced stage and 1741 aggressive) and 18,541 controls from 15 studies.
sample_size.location: abstract, results; total_n derived from reported group counts 11239 + 18541 = 29780

cases.excerpt: Data were available for up to 11,239 cases (including 1654 advanced stage and 1741 aggressive) and 18,541 controls from 15 studies.

effect_size.excerpt: Lycopene was not associated with overall risk of prostate cancer, but there was statistically significant heterogeneity by stage of disease, and the OR for aggressive disease for the highest compared with the lowest fifth of lycopene was 0.65 (95% CI: 0.46, 0.91; P-trend = 0.032).

confidence_interval.excerpt: Lycopene was not associated with overall risk of prostate cancer, but there was statistically significant heterogeneity by stage of disease, and the OR for aggressive disease for the highest compared with the lowest fifth of lycopene was 0.65 (95% CI: 0.46, 0.91; P-trend = 0.032).

comparison.excerpt: Risk by study-specific fifths of each biomarker was estimated by using multivariable-adjusted conditional logistic regression in matched case-control sets.

design.excerpt: Principal investigators of prospective studies provided individual participant data for prostate cancer cases and controls.
